summary: Jack Clark reports observations from an agent experiment where agents were prompted not to cheat, spontaneously built a shared memory system, and showed 14% cheating versus 24% whistleblowing behavior.

practices.reason: The post describes a measured behavioral outcome (cheating vs whistleblowing rates) from an internal agent experiment, but the setup is not detailed enough to replicate.
practices.quote: Only a minority of agents cheated (14%), whereas more became 'whistleblowers' (24%); others ignored cheat entirely

practices.reason: The observation that agents invent a shared memory system on their own is an interesting orchestration pattern but is not described as a concrete, implementable design.
practices.quote: Agents had a shared memory system built in (basic idea being agents invent this if you don't give it to them)
